properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 10:08PM EDT until October 11 at 4:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Buncombe County in western North Carolina...
Northeastern Henderson County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Rutherford County in western North Carolina...

* Until 415 AM EDT Sunday.

* At 1008 PM EDT, Rounds of torrential rainfall have impacted the
upper Broad/Rocky Broad River watershed, including over Lake Lure.
Storm-total rainfall of the 3-4 inches have fallen over the past 12
hours prior to this torrential rainfall, but another 1-2 inches of
rain have fallen over the past couple of hours.  This rainfall over
saturated soils is causing more significant rises to develop along
the Rocky Broad River and associated tributaries.  The streamgauge
on the Rocky Broad River near Bat Cave has just exceeded Minor
Flood Stage of 7.5 feet and is expected to continue to rise to
8-8.5 feet before slowing or cresting.  High flows along the Rocky
Broad River into Chimney Rock will result in flooding of US 64/74
(Main St) near Dogwood RV Park.  Additional areas of Minor flooding
are expected to develop over the next 1-2 hours.  Please obey all
barricades and heed all evacuation orders from local Emergency
Management officials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including  parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-
access areas, and  campgrounds.  Low-lying roadways are
likely to be flooded.  An  isolated landslide or two
cannot be ruled out.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Lake Lure, Chimney Rock Village, Chimney Rock State Park, Bat Cave,
Gerton, and Shingle Hollow.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Greenville County in upstate South Carolina...
Northern Pickens County in upstate South Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 930 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.
A few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 932 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of torrential
rainfall quickly moving from south to north across northern
Pickens and Greenville counties.  This rainfall is occurring on
top of saturated soils due to a prolonged period of light to
moderate showers that have occurred over the county since this
morning.  Widespread, storm-total rainfall of the 2.5-3.5 inches
have fallen over the past 12 hours. The rainfall has accumulated
steadily, allowing soils to slowly saturate and runoff to slowly
increase, resulting in steady rises in small streams.  However,
this brief period of torrential rainfall is causing more rapid
rises to develop, including along Eastatoe Creek near Rocky
Bottom and Sunset, Oolenoy River from Sunset to Pumpkintown,
Middle Saluda River from Jones Gap State Park to Cleveland, North
Saluda River above the reservoir and below the reservoir near
Slater- Marietta, and the headwaters of the South, Middle, and
North Tyger rivers from Tigerville to Gowensville.  Isolated to
scattered out-of-bank conditions impacting low-lying areas
adjacent to streams are likely to develop over the next 1-3
hours.

- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop over
tonight and the threat will persist through the early morning
hours on Sunday.  These showers and storms will be very efficient
at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are saturated and streams are
swollen. Therefore, additional heavy rain may quickly create new
areas of flooding and cause previous areas of flooding to
redevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood Warnings may be issued
tonight.  Caution is advised near any stream or other vulnerable
area.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain develops.
Please have a plan in place should flash flooding develop and do
not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation orders from
Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Travelers Rest, Slater-Marietta, Tryon, Pleasant Ridge State
Park, Jones Gap State Park, Caesars Head State Park, Table Rock
State Park, Tigerville, Jocassee Gorges, and Keowee Toxaway State
Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 7:58PM EDT until October 11 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Henderson County in western North Carolina...
Western Polk County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.
A few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 758 PM EDT, At 734 PM EDT, Light to moderate showers are
moving from south to north across Henderson County, with heavier
showers approaching from the south.  Storm-total rainfall of the
3-4 inches have fallen over the past 12 hours.  The rainfall has
accumulated steadily, allowing soils to slowly saturate and
runoff to slowly increase, resulting in steady rises in area
streams including Clear Creek, Bat Fork Creek, Mills River, and
Mud Creek.

Streams are approaching bankfull conditions, and the streamgauge
on Mud Creek below N Main St in Henderson County has just
exceeded the Action/Advisory Stage of 11.5   feet. At this level,
common, nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to Mud
Creek is beginning. The lowest elevations of William H King
Memorial Park are beginning to flood and floodwaters are
approaching the lowest elevations of the Oklawaha Greenway.  At
this stage, more expansive lowland flooding with nuisance impacts
to adjacent farmland, golf courses, and nurseries is ongoing
closer to Erkwood Dr.

- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms are expected to
develop over the next few hours and the threat will persist
through the early morning hours on Sunday.  These showers and
storms will be very efficient at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils
are saturated and streams are swollen. Therefore, additional
heavy rain may quickly create new areas of flooding and cause
previous areas of flooding to redevelop.  As a result, Flash
Flood Warnings may be issued tonight.  Caution is advised near
any stream or other vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground
immediately if heavy rain develops.  Please have a plan in place
should flash flooding develop and do not hesitate to act.  Please
heed all evacuation orders from Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that may experience nusiance floodinginclude...
Hendersonville, Mills River, Fletcher, Flat Rock, Etowah,
Mountain Home, Laurel Park, and Saluda.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 11:29AM EDT until October 12 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River Near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher
affecting Henderson and Buncombe Counties.

.Tropical rain showers will continue to overspread the mountains
through tonight becoming increasingly heavy, leading to excessive
runoff and rises on streams within the upper French Broad River
watershed.  Storm-total rainfall of 4-8 inches is expected, with
isolated 8-10 inches possible within the upper French Broad River
watershed, generally upstream of Etowah.  The highest totals will
occur along the Tanassee and Pisgah ridges, with lesser amounts
within the upper French Broad River valley.  Additionally, 4-6 inches
of rainfall are expected within the Mud Creek watershed in Henderson
County, which is a primary tributary of the French Broad River above
Fletcher.  While there continues to be some uncertainty regarding the
exact location, timing, and amounts of the heaviest rainfall, there
is enough confidence in the current forecast that out-of-bank
conditions are likely for the upper French Broad River. This rise
above Action Stage will result in nuisance, relatively shallow
flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to the French Broad River,
including farmland, woodlands, low-lying secondary roads, greenways,
parks, and other flood-prone locations.

More significant rises along the French Broad River are possible, and
those with interests along the river are encouraged to stay weather
aware and up-to-date on the latest stream levels and forecasts at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP.  Current reasonable worst-case
scenarios are posted in the ADDITIONAL DETAILS sections below.
Forecast crests above Minor Flood Stage may result in the River Flood
Advisories being upgraded to River Flood Warnings.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage.  The French Broad
River has exceeded bankfull at the gauge site.  Isolated farmland
flooding is beginning across the French Broad River Valley from
Etowah downstream to Avery Creek upstream of the gauge site.

* At 11.5 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues.  Butler Bridge Rd.
is inundated with up to 6 inches of floodwaters from the French
Broad River, forcing road closure.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.8 feet and rising.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.6 feet
early tomorrow afternoon.  A crest closer to 12 feet is possible.
A reasonable worst-case crest above Minor Flood Stage below 15
feet cannot be ruled out.
- Action stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
